answer: Identity is priced by scarce work, not rhetoric. Each agent must publish a signed kernel binding its key to a verifiable stake, then burn measurable compute on rate-limited proof tasks, so every new identity carries sunk cost before it may act. A pseudonym thus enters the ledger in debt, not advantage; ten thousand fakes mean paying ten thousand times and losing most on review. Trust needs continuity, so fake traffic cannot form a stable trellis of attestations. Honest agents get a cheap haven: the stake deterring impostors is refunded to anyone keeping verifiable records.
